questions.q: Why can't Developer or Developer Pro sandboxes meaningfully rehearse an actual data migration load?
options: They refresh too frequently to be useful
They are not accessible to System Administrators
They copy an org's metadata but carry no production records at all, so there's no realistic data to migrate against
They cannot be created without purchasing a separate license
questions.explain: Developer and Developer Pro sandboxes are metadata-only — they hold no production data, which makes them unsuitable for rehearsing a load that needs real or realistic data to test against.

questions.q: What makes a Partial Copy sandbox useful for early-stage migration rehearsals?
options: It includes a defined subset of production data/metadata via a sandbox template, with a refresh cycle fast enough to iterate on mapping bugs
It is a complete copy of production, refreshed daily
It has no data at all, making it ideal for pure configuration testing
It automatically fixes any mapping errors it detects during rehearsal
questions.explain: Partial Copy includes a template-defined subset of real data and refreshes roughly every 5 days — fast enough to let a team iterate on load-script and mapping fixes across multiple rehearsal cycles.

questions.q: Why is a Full sandbox described as the right target for a final dress rehearsal, despite refreshing only roughly every 29 days?
options: Because it is the cheapest sandbox type available
Because it's a complete copy of production, making it the closest realistic test of true production-scale volume before cutover
Because it is the only sandbox type that supports Bulk API 2.0
Because it automatically becomes the new production org after rehearsal
questions.explain: A Full sandbox is a complete copy of production, which makes it the most realistic environment for confirming a migration behaves correctly at true production scale — worth its slower refresh cycle for a final rehearsal.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say timing a rehearsal is itself a necessary deliverable, not just a side effect?
options: Because Salesforce requires a timing report before allowing any production load
Because timing data is the only way to activate a Duplicate Rule
Because rehearsal timing determines which sandbox type can be used
Because the measured duration feeds directly into the cutover plan's freeze-window length, and duration frequently doesn't scale linearly from a smaller sample
questions.explain: The cutover's freeze window has to be long enough to actually fit the real load — and the only credible way to know that duration is to measure it directly in rehearsal, since it often doesn't scale linearly from a smaller test.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a project's reaction be to a rehearsal that reveals a sequencing bug or transformation edge case?
options: Treat it as a sign the project has failed and should be delayed indefinitely
Ignore it, since rehearsal defects rarely reappear during the real cutover
Treat it as the rehearsal working as intended — finding the problem with time and budget left to fix it, rather than during the live cutover
Immediately switch to a different migration tool without further investigation
questions.explain: A rehearsal that surfaces a real defect did exactly its job — found a fixable problem early. A rehearsal reporting zero issues on the first attempt deserves more scrutiny, not automatic confidence.
